title: camera_image_get
description: A device on the hub path (parental controls or the effective rule control_path hub; never a watch) asks for the current still image of a camera; other devices read it from Home Assistant with their own key. The hub reads GET /api/camera_proxy/<entity_id> and answers camera_image with the same request_id. The hub answers in this order: (1) a malformed request (also a width outside 64-3840, or a request_id of a request of this device still open) → control_error {invalid_request}, the open request continues; (2) not a paired, active device on the hub path, or a watch → control_error {not_hub_controlled}; (3) access closed, an unknown entity, an entity of another domain or outside the device's scope (placed in one of its readable areas, or the run target of such a tile) → control_error {not_visible}, the same answer in every case and before Home Assistant is contacted or a kids rule is read; (4) a request for this entity still open, more than one per second for this entity, or the device's image budget used up (x-limits hub_image_*), or a lower share the hub enforces → control_error {rate_limited, retry_after}; (5) with parental controls a blocked device type (kids_blocked_types) → rule_blocked {reason blocked}; (6) the hub reads the image from Home Assistant with its own access, without following a redirect: an error answer, a redirect, no image, more than 2 MiB or a type other than JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF → control_error {ha_error}, Home Assistant not reachable → {ha_unavailable}. The content type is normalized: lower case, parameters dropped, image/jpg and image/pjpeg are image/jpeg. The answer carries the image only: never a URL, a Home Assistant token or a signed image URL. The hub keeps no copy. Live video is not part of the hub path. The app asks again while the tile or the detail view is visible. These limits are maxima: a hub may enforce lower shares (for example of a hub-wide limit of open reads) and answer rate_limited earlier; clients honor rate_limited with retry_after at any time. The app asks when the state's attributes.hub_picture_id appears or changes ($defs/hub_picture_id); without it it asks for nothing.

entity_id.description: A camera entity; any other entity is answered with not_visible.

width.description: Optional hint, best effort: the width the app needs, in pixels. The hub passes width=<width> and height=<ceil(width*9/16)> to Home Assistant's camera proxy. Home Assistant then scales a JPEG image down (only when its libjpeg-turbo is available) by the smallest of the factors 7/8, 3/4, 5/8, 1/2, 3/8, 1/4, 1/8 that keeps the image at least that wide and that high, so the image may be up to about twice as wide; it never scales up, and other formats or an image already smaller come unscaled. A camera integration may use the size itself. The hub does not scale (it has no image library). The 2 MiB limit applies either way.
